content.comment_body: I'm looking to use a [product_name] device to measure oil temperature and trigger an alarm once the temperature reaches around 180°F. There's already a type J thermocouple installed. What do I need to connect the type J thermocouple? Should I switch to a PT100/1000 sensor? I'm using a [article_no] device and an [product_name] module. The sensor is a type J thermocouple.

The [product_name] system can only read PT100/1000 sensors on an [product_name] RTD module, not thermocouples. Thermocouples can be connected to a 0-10V analog input, but since their response isn’t linear, you would need to manually adjust the readings through calculations, which consumes a lot of programming blocks. It’s more practical to use an external transmitter for thermocouples that outputs a 0-10V or 0/4-20mA signal.
Thanks for the quick reply. I'll look for a PT100 sensor with similar mechanical features.

analysis.insight_summary: The user wants to monitor oil temperature using a [company_name] automation device with an existing type J thermocouple and trigger an alarm at a set value. Responses point out that the [product_name] module only natively supports PT100/1000 sensors, not thermocouples. While manual connection and calibration are technically possible through analog input and custom calculations, this method requires substantial programming and external hardware, making it impractical. The user agrees and decides to obtain a compatible PT100 sensor instead.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to connect a type J thermocouple directly to the automation module for temperature measurement and automatic alarm triggering, without requiring manual calibration or additional external components.
